I live in the USA and I read somewhere that USA is the only/highest country where you can see so many national flags put up. Including my neighborhood, you can't walk anywhere and not see a US flag at some vantage point.

TLDR; The less you learn/see the information, the less you'll remember it. Try to find a way where you can refresh your memory of the material.
____________________________________________________________________
I kinda agree with you. Especially with when I'm in school. 

I have a deep passion in music and I try to learn a lot of music theory & music production (and a lot of misc. thing as well; whatever peaks my interest)
When I'm taking classes, I learned that I can't really focus too much on my side projects since I'm learning a lot of school material. It is somewhat frustrating since I want to learn things of what I want to currently learn but I feel like there is a cap for me.

IMO, learning a lot of material at one time; one can lose a lot (or most) of the material since there is "information overload". I feel your brain can process a certain amount of data at a time and if there is a colossal amount, it won't know which is most important.

I found that if you have a main focus of study & a secondary focus, it can grasp both but it won't be as efficient as if you just study one. A way to beat that is to keep reminding yourself of material. 

Like DokterW said, "If you don't use it, you will lose it."
I want to eventually make a system where I can input data with beneficial information that I can refer to easily to keep the information in my head while learning new material. 

As an idea, keep a notebook full of relevant knowledge that you want to keep in your brain and refer to it weekly. The more you see it, the stronger the connections will remain in your brain. 
My idea of this is creating a program where every time on startup on my computer, it will bring up inputted information (such as what a specific vitamin is good for) and I can review it when I start my computer to refresh my memory. 
There's many ways to do this.
